grantee: David Humbird (contractor, commissioned by Open Philanthropy)
title: Scale-up economics for cultured meat
key_findings: Techno-economic analysis finding that slow cell growth, metabolic inefficiency, contamination safeguards and costly media would likely keep cultured meat from being affordable as food. Cheaper plant hydrolysate media and better metabolic efficiency are necessary but not sufficient.
key_numbers: Fed-batch: $37/kg wet cell mass, 6.8 kTA, total capital investment $328 M; perfusion: $51/kg, 6.9 kTA, total capital investment $663 M; fed-batch with hydrolysate media at $2/kg: $22/kg; affordability target ~$25/kg wet cell mass. Base year for costs not stated (input prices from 2020 sources).
link_to_grant: Funding statement: analysis funded by Open Philanthropy; Coefficient Giving research page says Open Philanthropy commissioned it.
notes: Not one of the 61 listed grants (a commissioned contract); research page https://coefficientgiving.org/research/scale-up-economics-for-cultured-meat/ dated 7 June 2021. Numbers read from the PDF on the Coefficient Giving site.

title: Plant-Based versus Conventional Meat: Substitution, Complementarity, and Market Impacts
authors: Vincenzina Caputo, Jayson L. Lusk, Dan Blaustein-Rejto
key_findings: US surveys find plant-based meat and conventional meat act mostly as complements at home, with mixed results in restaurants; price cuts for plant-based meat would barely change cattle or chicken production.
key_numbers: Home survey n=1,011; restaurant survey n=999; a 5% plant-based beef price cut changes farm-level cattle by +0.02% (home) and -0.06% (restaurants); restaurant own-price elasticity for plant-based burgers 1.490 (survey data August 2023).
link_to_grant: Funding statement says the work was partly funded by Open Philanthropy and Breakthrough Institute.
notes: Year from survey date; PDF undated.

title: Alternative Proteins and Asia
authors: Food Frontier with Mintel and Te Puna Whakaaronui
key_findings: Of 11 Asian markets assessed, the five most promising for alternative proteins are China, Singapore, South Korea, Japan and Thailand; taste, price and perceived processing are the main barriers.
key_numbers: Flexitarians 19% on average across the top five markets (China 24%, Singapore 21%, South Korea 9%, Japan 3%, Thailand 38%); based on 5,000 consumers (2023).
link_to_grant: Grantee publication on the grant topic within the grant period; the report pages do not name the funder.
notes: Released 25 July 2023. Food Frontier's own pages checked do not mention Vietnam.

title: Documentary films can increase public interest in plant-based diets in the USA
authors: Anna T. Thomas, Jessica E. Hope, Maya B. Mathur
key_findings: Attention to food documentaries raised online searches for plant-based food, but this did not show up as measurable consumption.
key_numbers: Searches up to 43% higher the following week per one standard deviation increase in searches for the film (US).
link_to_grant: Acknowledgements cite a gift from Open Philanthropy supporting two authors.
notes: Published 19 September 2025; linked to CG-G044 by grantee and period, not confirmed as this specific grant. Consumer research, not supply side.

title: Technical feasibility of egg ingredient reduction/replacement in US foods
key_findings: Maps US branded foods containing egg by egg volume, egg function and replacement difficulty; no category is easy, and subs and sandwiches, wraps and burritos, snack bars and pasta are suggested targets.
key_numbers: About 80% of sampled products moderately difficult and about 20% difficult to replace; processed eggs approximately 8% of global egg production; US ~26% of 108 billion total eggs; product data 2019 to 2025.
link_to_grant: Report states it was commissioned by Coefficient Giving (formerly Open Philanthropy).
notes: Not one of the 61 listed grants. Cites an IMPROVE (2023) study that may be the output of CG-G023. Dated 14 December 2025.
